title: Couscous de sorgho (Nyri digari, Red or White Sorghum Couscous)
author: Tata Ngome et al. (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré)
desc: Sorghum flour couscous made like the maize one: a flour ‘milk’ cooked about 10 minutes after the boil returns, then the flour added and cooked 10 more minutes; served hot with a sauce.
longDesc: p. 19 of the October 2023 recipe book. Sorghum flour (red or white; plain, soaked or not soaked); quantities not printed. The method follows the maize couscous (CMR053) with about 10 minutes after the boil returns, then the flour is stirred in and cooked a further 10 minutes. The page notes the meal must be served hot with a sauce.
ingredients: Sorghum flour (red or white) — quantity not printed
Cold water for the ‘milk’ — quantity not printed
steps: Boil water. Mix a little flour with cold water into a ‘milk’.
Pour the ‘milk’ into the boiling water, stirring. Cook about 10 minutes after the boil returns.
chefTips: The printed note is that this meal must be served hot with a sauce.
Soaked and unsoaked flour are both given as routes.
commonMistakes: Not stirring while the flour goes in.
Treating the times as a ratio guide.
healthBenefits: Sorghum is a gluten-free whole grain staple.
culturalNote: The book attributes its recipes to the northern part of Cameroon and names no community, lamidat or town for any recipe.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Couscous de sorgho rouge ou blanc (Nyri digari)’ (p. 19). Authors as printed: ‘Tata Ngome et al.’ (CIFOR-ICRAF, IRAD, Université de Ngaoundéré; ReSI-NoC project); October 2023 (V1), © 2024, CC BY 4.0. Yield not printed for any recipe in the book. Servings 4 and prep are placeholders. TWO-PASS.
